fatal_errors: The proposed nanoflake surface coating does not reconstruct the target intervention, which was increasing Mo content within SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 bulk composites.

The cited evidence concerns a coating on a steel-on-steel tribopair tested only in ambient conditions; it does not support effectiveness on high-entropy-alloy substrates across cryogenic-to-high temperatures.
The claimed broad-temperature reductions in both friction and wear are quantitative extrapolations without supporting temperature-dependent evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses self-lubrication and offers a genuinely distinct, testable coating strategy, but it has little agreement with the hidden paper. It omits Mo-dependent FCC lattice distortion, sigma-phase strengthening, the Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite architecture, SPS processing, the specified room-temperature-to-800 °C test conditions, and the transition from low-temperature sulfide/Ag lubrication to high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation. Its baseline is an undefined untreated HEA rather than Mo0.2, and its boundaries lack concrete temperatures, loads, counterface, atmosphere, and sliding distance. The proposed controlled ball-on-disk comparison, profilometry, microscopy, and explicit falsification criterion are reasonably discriminating, although the requirement for improvement at every temperature and load is overly broad. The evidence validates good ambient tribology of the nanoflake coating on steel, but not the central wide-temperature claim or transfer to an HEA substrate.
